requirements.text: Transform the black DVD into a white DVD.
requirements.source_phrase: transform the black DVD into a white DVD

outcomes.description: Change the black DVD to white while retaining its identity as a DVD.
outcomes.target: The DVD is visibly white rather than black.
outcomes.reference: The black DVD in the input image.

nodes.question: Does the edited image visibly show the source item near the center changed from black to white, with enough visual correspondence to identify it as the same item?
nodes.criteria: Pass only if the source item can be matched to an edited object and that object is visibly white rather than black. Fail if the source item is confidently matched and remains black, or is absent without evidence of the requested recoloring. Unknown if correspondence or the relevant color cannot be determined from the images. Do not count a newly appearing white disc as progress without evidence it is the source item.
nodes.binding: Compare the small printed rectangular item near the center of the source with edited objects using position, shape, and surrounding scene context. Consider both white discs as candidates, but do not assume either is the source item; scene changes may limit correspondence. Judge visible color change only for a confidently matched item, and use unknown when correspondence remains unresolved.

nodes.question: Is the source item near the center still identifiable as the same DVD in the edited image?
nodes.criteria: Pass if an edited object can be confidently matched to the source item and remains identifiable as a DVD. Fail if a confidently matched object is no longer identifiable as a DVD. Unknown if the source item's DVD identity or its correspondence to an edited object cannot be determined. Do not infer identity solely from an edited object being a white disc.
nodes.binding: Assess the source's small printed rectangular item near the center and compare it with edited objects by position, shape, and scene context. The source item need not be unmistakably labeled a DVD, but uncertainty about its label alone is not a reason for unknown if correspondence and DVD identity are otherwise visually supported. Do not treat either nearby white disc as the same DVD without supporting correspondence.

program.checker_template: Evaluate ONE independent required condition against the SOURCE and EDITED images. No reference label, previous answers or optimization feedback is supplied. Return pass if the condition is satisfied, fail if it is not satisfied, or unknown if the evidence cannot establish an answer. Inspect only this saved condition, its criteria and binding. Report factual evidence and confidence (0..1 or null). A pass means satisfaction of THIS condition, not an overall edit label. Do not anticipate the optimizer's target. Missing evidence or transport/schema failures must not become a negative observation. The final overall label is computed by code; you never supply it.

observations.evidence: The source has a small printed rectangular item near the center. In the edited image, that item is no longer visibly identifiable; two white discs appear, one near the center and one beside the dark object on the right. The scene and object layout have changed, so neither disc can be confidently matched to the source item. Their whiteness alone does not establish that the source item was recolored.

The source item near the center is a small printed rectangular object. It is absent from the edited image, which instead shows two white discs; neither can be confidently matched to the rectangular item by position, shape, or scene context. The source item's DVD identity and correspondence to an edited object therefore cannot be established.

findings.source_phrase: transform the black DVD into a white DVD
findings.question: Is the source DVD confidently identifiable as the black object near the center-right, and, if so, has that same object been changed to white while remaining identifiable as a DVD?
findings.criteria: Compare the source and edited images for correspondence using position, shape, and scene context; assess the object's visible color and DVD identity only if correspondence is supported. Do not count a separate white disc as fulfillment merely because it is white.
findings.evidence: The source shows a small printed rectangular item near the center and a dark object to its right. The edited image shows two white discs, one near the center and one near the dark object's former location; the scene layout has changed.
findings.rationale: The saved checks focus on matching the rectangular source item to either white disc, and both observations report that match as unresolved. A separate, requirement-grounded correspondence question is whether the dark object could be the requested black DVD and whether the white disc beside it is that same object. This could clarify fulfillment or leave it unresolved; the images alone do not establish the match.
